findings.reason: without a followup naming §14 no coordinator is told to build it, and it would stall behind a plan that reads as fully routed.
findings.text: §14 is freshly declared `implementable` in `plan-section-declarations` (line 24), but the only open followup, `f-araiid-009`, names §8, §11, §10, §12, §13 and §6 and does not name §14, so the plan's newest implementable section has no dispatch route

findings.reason: a §6 measurement taken before §14 lands is stale the moment §14 merges, and the plan's success criterion would be asserted against a superseded tree.
findings.text: §6's deliverable re-measures after "§2 to §5 and the read fixes §8, §10, §11, §12 and §13", omitting §14, which changes `resolve_resource`/identification on the very roadmap read path §6 measures (§14's own Why: "Every slug resolve whose memo is cold pays this cost: a dispatch, an MCP read and a roadmap"), so the section repeats the stale-and-incomplete dependency list a prior review already corrected once for §8–§13

findings.reason: two implementable sections editing `resources.py` with no declared edge can be dispatched concurrently and lose one node's edits at merge.
findings.text: §14 writes `reckon/resources.py`, the same file §12 writes (still `implementable`, and its own text says "This section runs after §8 and §10, because it also writes `resources.py`"), yet §14 declares no ordering relative to §12, unlike every other section that shares a file

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `picker._resolved_plan_path` (reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:125), `resources.resolve_resource` (reckon/resources.py:728), `_canonical_identity_is_unique` (reckon/resources.py:690), `identify_resource` (reckon/resources.py:276), `_identify_meta` (reckon/resources.py:263), `parse_meta` (reckon/_plan_html.py:2204), commit `ec53f8f61` (fix(plans): make the record fast path defer to the parser, 2026-09-26) and the plan `lane-and-model-routing.html` all resolve; `health-tool-latency/scripts/profile_reads.py` resolves under the health-review report directory cited in §1.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every changed section names a negative control that makes the guarded thing happen (`s6`'s base arm must exceed the deadline; `s14`'s control routes identification back through the full `parse_meta` and requires the zero-entry case to fail).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — `s6` writes to the run's log directory and `s14` to the run's log directory; neither names a node-local or session-scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `s14` and `s6` name no plan, sprint or ticket label in code symbols or filenames; the commit and run ids they cite are plan-doc citations, not source names.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §14's root cause matches its evidence (verified: `_parse_meta_uncached` calls `read_state` for a record-carrying document, `reckon/_plan_html.py:2274`, introduced by `ec53f8f61`), its mechanism produces its done-when, and its production caller is named (`_canonical_identity_is_unique` through `_resolved_plan_path`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — `s6` delivers one measurement, `s14` one change (identification reads head only).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §14 is declared `implementable` but appears in no followup, so it has no dispatch route.
